They attained such happiness as is experienced by one who has entered the third <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption). And at that very time, they were endowed with such a form of wisdom that <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> residing in other <s>Buddha</s>-fields uttered this solemn utterance (<s>udāna</s>): 'Well done is restraint! Well done is tranquility! Well done is self-control! Well done is the living of the celibate life! Well done is non-harming toward beings who have come into being!' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, seated on that very lion-throne, outshining this <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> (billion-world) world-system, stood blazing, shining, and radiant with splendor, complexion, glory, and majesty. In the eastern direction, the southern, western, northern, below, above, and in the intermediate directions, outshining world-systems [as numerous] as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river, the <s>Tathāgata</s> stood blazing, shining, and radiant with splendor, complexion, glory, and majesty. Just as <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, outshines all mountains and stands blazing, shining, and radiant with splendor, complexion, glory, and majesty — even so the <s>Bhagavān</s>, outshining all world-systems, stood blazing, shining, and radiant with splendor, complexion, glory, and majesty. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> again displayed to the beings of the <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> world-system a bodily form just as natural and similar to theirs — the same kind of form as theirs.
